def-fdmath-finite-ensemble-and-covarianc:
## Definition

Let $N\ge1$ be an integer and let $a_1,\ldots,a_N\in[0,\infty)$ satisfy $\sum_{j=1}^N a_j=1$. The fixed tuple $(a_1,\ldots,a_N)$ is a finite ensemble of weights. For $X=(X_1,\ldots,X_N)$ with $X_j\in\mathbb R^m$, define its weighted mean and its $j$th fluctuation by

$$\bar X:=\sum_{j=1}^N a_jX_j,\qquad X'_j:=X_j-\bar X.$$

For $Y=(Y_1,\ldots,Y_N)$ with $Y_j\in\mathbb R^n$ and the same weights, define the cross-covariance tensor

$$C(X,Y):=\sum_{j=1}^N a_j X'_j\otimes Y'_j\in\mathbb R^{m\times n},$$

where $x\otimes y$ is the matrix with entries $(x\otimes y)_{rs}=x_r y_s$. The covariance tensor of $X$ is $C(X):=C(X,X)$. For finite families of functions with values in these Euclidean spaces, these definitions apply pointwise using the same fixed weights at each point. No probability space, limiting operation, or interpretation as an empirical sample is part of this definition.
thm-fdmath-finite-reynolds-identity:
## Statement

Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open interval, let $d,N\ge1$ be integers, let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be open, and fix constants $a_j\ge0$ with $\sum_{j=1}^N a_j=1$ and a common $\nu\ge0$. For $j=1,\ldots,N$, let $u_j:I\times\Omega\to\mathbb R^d$ be continuously differentiable in $(t,x)$ with continuous second spatial derivatives, let $p_j:I\times\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be continuously differentiable, and let $f_j:I\times\Omega\to\mathbb R^d$ be continuous. Suppose pointwise that

$$\operatorname{div}u_j=0,\qquad \partial_tu_j+\operatorname{div}(u_j\otimes u_j)+\nabla p_j=\nu\Delta u_j+f_j.$$

Here $(u\otimes v)_{rs}=u_rv_s$, $\operatorname{div}$ of a matrix field is rowwise, $(\operatorname{div}A)_r=\sum_{s=1}^d\partial_{x_s}A_{rs}$, and $\Delta$ acts componentwise. Define the weighted means $\bar u=\sum_j a_ju_j$, $\bar p=\sum_j a_jp_j$, and $\bar f=\sum_j a_jf_j$, the fluctuations $v_j=u_j-\bar u$, and the covariance tensor $R=\sum_j a_jv_j\otimes v_j$. Then, pointwise on $I\times\Omega$,

$$\operatorname{div}\bar u=0,\qquad \sum_{j=1}^N a_jv_j=0,\qquad \sum_{j=1}^N a_j u_j\otimes u_j=\bar u\otimes\bar u+R,$$

and the exact averaged equation is

$$\partial_t\bar u+\operatorname{div}(\bar u\otimes\bar u)+\nabla\bar p=\nu\Delta\bar u+\bar f-\operatorname{div}R.$$

The tensor $R$ is symmetric positive semidefinite, with $z^{\mathsf T}Rz=\sum_j a_j(v_j\cdot z)^2\ge0$ for every $z\in\mathbb R^d$. With $\operatorname{tr}A:=\sum_{r=1}^d A_{rr}$ for $A\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}$, the pointwise energy split is $\sum_j a_j|u_j|^2=|\bar u|^2+\operatorname{tr}R$. These are identities for the specified smooth functions; they assert neither existence of such solutions nor a statistical or physical interpretation.
thm-fdmath-mean-fluctuation-energy-trans:
## Statement

Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open interval, let $d\ge2$ and $N\ge1$ be integers, and define the flat torus $\mathbb T^d:=(\mathbb R/2\pi\mathbb Z)^d$, with integration using Lebesgue measure on a periodic cell $[0,2\pi]^d$. Fix constants $a_j\ge0$ with $\sum_{j=1}^N a_j=1$ and a common constant $\nu\ge0$. For $j=1,\ldots,N$, let $u_j:I\times\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d$ be continuously differentiable in $(t,x)$ with continuous second spatial derivatives, and let $p_j:I\times\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ be continuously differentiable. Require these fields to be $2\pi$-periodic in each spatial coordinate, so they descend to $\mathbb T^d$. Suppose they are unforced and satisfy pointwise on $I\times\mathbb R^d$

$$\operatorname{div}u_j=0,\qquad \partial_tu_j+\operatorname{div}(u_j\otimes u_j)+\nabla p_j=\nu\Delta u_j.$$

Use $(u\otimes v)_{rs}=u_rv_s$, $(\operatorname{div}A)_r=\sum_s\partial_{x_s}A_{rs}$ for a matrix field $A$, and componentwise Laplacian. For $A\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}$ set $\operatorname{tr}A:=\sum_rA_{rr}$. Define $\bar u=\sum_j a_ju_j$, $v_j=u_j-\bar u$, $R=\sum_j a_jv_j\otimes v_j$, and

$$E_m(t):=\frac12\int_{\mathbb T^d}|\bar u(t,x)|^2\,dx,\qquad E_f(t):=\frac12\int_{\mathbb T^d}\operatorname{tr}R(t,x)\,dx=\frac12\int_{\mathbb T^d}\sum_j a_j|v_j(t,x)|^2\,dx.$$

For a matrix $A$ and vector field $q$, set $A:\nabla q:=\sum_{r,s=1}^d A_{rs}\partial_{x_s}q_r$ and $|\nabla q|^2:=\sum_{r,s=1}^d|\partial_{x_s}q_r|^2$. Then for every $t\in I$,

$$\frac{dE_m}{dt}=-\nu\int_{\mathbb T^d}|\nabla\bar u|^2\,dx+\int_{\mathbb T^d}R:\nabla\bar u\,dx,$$

$$\frac{dE_f}{dt}=-\nu\int_{\mathbb T^d}\sum_j a_j|\nabla v_j|^2\,dx-\int_{\mathbb T^d}R:\nabla\bar u\,dx.$$

For every $t_0<t_1$ in $I$, the endpoint identities are

$$E_m(t_1)-E_m(t_0)=-\nu\int_{t_0}^{t_1}\int_{\mathbb T^d}|\nabla\bar u|^2\,dx\,dt+\int_{t_0}^{t_1}\int_{\mathbb T^d}R:\nabla\bar u\,dx\,dt,$$

$$E_f(t_1)-E_f(t_0)=-\nu\int_{t_0}^{t_1}\int_{\mathbb T^d}\sum_j a_j|\nabla v_j|^2\,dx\,dt-\int_{t_0}^{t_1}\int_{\mathbb T^d}R:\nabla\bar u\,dx\,dt.$$

The transfer term has opposite signs in the two balances and cancels in their sum. No sign is asserted for $\int_{\mathbb T^d}R:\nabla\bar u\,dx$.
